gloss: be old; old, an old man, elder; beard; old age
summary: Old age and the old man, above all the old man as elder. The verb is to be or grow old, said of Abraham and Sarah, Isaac, Joshua, Eli, Samuel and David as their days drew to a close; the adjective זָקֵן is old, and as a noun an old man and an elder: the old men of Israel, of a city, of Egypt or Moab, who sat in the gate, judged, gave counsel and stood for the people before Moses, the judges and the kings. The noun זָקָן is the beard, cut or plucked in mourning and shame, and זִקְנָה, זְקֻנִים and זֹקֶן are old age. The beard is the root's meaning in every cognate language, and Arabic has from the same root a word for an extremely old man, so “old” may first have been “bearded”, the grown man; scripture does not say so.

words.summary: About 180 times, two thirds of them “the elders”, mostly “the elders of Israel” or “of the city”. The brief's 15 qal tokens under this key are the stative verb (זָקֵן “he was old”), spelled alike.

senses.gloss: old, aged; an old man or woman
senses.definition: Having lived many days: the old as against the young, an old man or (feminine) an old woman; old and full of days at death; the old honoured for their gray hair.

evidence.note: “Abraham and Sarah were זְקֵנִים, come into days; the way of women had ceased to be with Sarah.”
“The splendour of young men is their strength, and the adornment of זְקֵנִים is gray hair (שֵׂיבָה).”
“Rise before gray hair, and honour the face of a זָקֵן, and fear your God: I am Yahweh.”
“Old men and old women (זְקֵנִים וּזְקֵנוֹת) shall again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand from many days.”
The men of Sodom, “from young to old (מִנַּעַר וְעַד־זָקֵן)”.
“Young men and also virgins, זְקֵנִים with youths.”
“Then the virgin shall rejoice in the dance, and young men and old together.”
Abraham died “in a good old age, זָקֵן and satisfied”.
Isaac died “זָקֵן וּשְׂבַע יָמִים”, old and full of days.
“Job died, old and full of days.”
“We have an old father, and a son of his old age, a little one.”
“An old man coming from his work in the field at evening.”
“An old prophet dwelt in Bethel.”
“A nation fierce of face, which will not lift up the face for the old, nor show favour to the young.”
To Babylon: “on the old you made your yoke very heavy.”
“Young and old lie on the ground in the streets.”
“No more an infant of days, or a זָקֵן who does not fill his days.”
“Your זְקֵנִים shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions” (Joel 2:28 in English Bibles); quoted at Act 2:17.
Peter quotes Joel: “your old men (πρεσβύτεροι) shall dream dreams.”

senses.gloss: the old, looked to for wisdom
senses.definition: The old as those expected to know and to counsel, so that it is notable when the young understand more, or when the old do not understand.

evidence.note: Elihu waited to speak to Job “because they were older (זְקֵנִים) than he”.
“It is not the great who are wise, nor the old (זְקֵנִים) who understand judgment.”
“I understand more than the elders, for I have kept your precepts.”
“He takes away the discernment of the elders.”
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the elders” for that of the young men (יְלָדִים) who grew up with him.
“Law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.”

senses.definition: An old man holding standing among his people: the elders of Israel, of a tribe, a city or a house, who represented the people, sat in the gate as judges and witnesses, gave counsel, and acted for the people with Moses, the judges and the kings; also the elders of other nations, and of the priests.

evidence.note: “Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know that they are elders of the people and its officers.”
The parents bring a rebellious son “to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place”.
Boaz “took ten men of the elders of the city and said, Sit here”: witnesses at the gate (Rut 4:9, 11).
“Her husband is known in the gates, when he sits with the elders of the land.”
“Go and gather the elders of Israel, and say to them, Yahweh the God of your fathers has appeared to me.”
“Come up to Yahweh, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu and seventy of the elders of Israel.”
“The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.”
Moses gave the law “to the priests the sons of Levi … and to all the elders of Israel”.
Israel served Yahweh “all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua”.
“The elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah.”
“All the elders of Israel gathered and came to Samuel at Ramah”, asking for a king.
“All the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron … and they anointed David king over Israel.”
Rehoboam took counsel “with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father”.
“The men of his city, the elders and the nobles who dwelt in his city”, condemned Naboth.
“The elders of his house and all the elders of the land of Egypt”.
Abraham's servant “זְקַן בֵּיתוֹ, who ruled over all that he had”: the elder of his house.
“The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went.”
Hezekiah sent “the elders of the priests” to Isaiah.
“The elders of Gebal and her wise men were in you, repairing your seams”: the skilled old men of a guild.
“Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel” offering incense to images.
“Men of the elders of Israel came to inquire of Yahweh.”
Among the stays of Jerusalem: “judge and prophet, diviner and elder”.
“The elder and the honoured of face, he is the head; the prophet who teaches lies, he is the tail.”
Joseph was “to bind his princes at his will and teach his elders wisdom”.
“Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the seat of the elders.”
“Princes are hung up by their hands; the faces of elders are not honoured.”
“The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music.”
“The elders of every city, and its judges.”
“Yahweh of Armies will reign in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders, glory.”
Jesus must “suffer many things from the elders (πρεσβυτέρων) and chief priests and scribes”.
“Rulers of the people and elders of Israel”: the same body in the apostles' day.

“Rulers of the people and elders (πρεσβύτεροι) of Israel.”
The centurion “sent to him elders of the Jews”.
Paul and Barnabas “appointed them elders in every church”.
“By it the elders (οἱ πρεσβύτεροι) obtained a good report”: the men of old.
“Twenty-four elders sitting, clothed in white garments.”

evidence.locator: Gen.25.8, זָקֵן → πρεσβύτης; Jdg.19.16, זָקֵן → πρεσβύτης; πρεσβύτης renders זָקֵן ×16

evidence.locator: Exo.12.21, זִקְנֵי → γερουσία; Deu.25.7, זְקֵנִים → γερουσία; γερουσία renders זָקֵן ×7

evidence.note: “The council and all the senate (γερουσίαν) of the sons of Israel.”

parallels.note: “Gray hair”: the old man's mark and adornment.
“Officer”: the elders and the officers of the people together.
“Prince, chief”: princes and elders, the leading men.

opposites.note: “Youth, boy”: from young to old, all the people.
“Young man”: strength against gray hair, visions against dreams.
“Child, young man”: the counsel of the elders against that of the young men.

words.summary: About 25 times, a stative verb whose perfect זָקֵן is spelled as the adjective. The brief's 20 tokens with no stem under this key are the adjective.

senses.definition: To have lived many days, or to come to that: said of the patriarchs, judges and kings as their lives drew to a close, often with “come into days” or “full of days”, and with the failing that goes with it: dim eyes, heaviness, cold, the end of childbearing, death near.

evidence.note: “I have been young (נַעַר), and now am old (זָקַנְתִּי), yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken.”
Samuel: “I am old and gray (זָקַנְתִּי וָשַׂבְתִּי) … I have walked before you from my youth to this day.”
Isaac: “Behold, I am old; I do not know the day of my death.”
Sarah: “After I am worn out shall I have pleasure, and my lord is old?”
“Shall I truly bear, and I am old?”
“Our father is old, and there is no man in the earth to come in to us.”
“Abraham was old, come into days, and Yahweh had blessed Abraham in all things.”
“Isaac was old, and his eyes were too dim to see.”
“You are old, come into days, and there remains very much land to possess.”
Joshua: “I am old, come into days.”
Eli died, “for the man was old and heavy”.
“Behold, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways: now appoint us a king.”
“King David was old, come into days; they covered him with clothes, but he was not warm.”
“Barzillai was very old, eighty years old.”
Naomi: “I am too old to have a husband.”
“Do not despise your mother when she is old.”
“David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.”
“Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and died; he was a hundred and thirty years old.”

senses.definition: To come to old age, of a man trained in his youth, and of the root of a felled tree.

evidence.note: “Train a youth according to his way; even when he is old (יַזְקִין) he will not depart from it.”
“Though its root grow old in the earth, and its stump die in the ground”, at the scent of water it will bud; but man dies and lies prostrate (Job 14:10).

evidence.locator: Gen.27.2, זָקַנְתִּי → γεγήρακα; Job.14.8, יַזְקִין → γηράσῃ

evidence.note: “When you are old (γηράσῃς), you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you.”

parallels.note: “Be full of days”: old and full of days, at the end of life.

opposites.note: “Youth”: I have been young and now am old.

words.summary: About 19 times. The meaning every cognate language shares. The brief's token at Gen 24:2 (זְקַן בֵּיתוֹ) is the adjective “the elder of his house”, filed here by spelling.

senses.definition: The hair of a man's chin and cheeks, beside the hair of the head; not to be marred at its corners, anointed with Aaron's oil, a place for infection.

evidence.note: “A man or a woman with an infection on the head or in the beard.”
“He shall shave all his hair: his head and his beard and his eyebrows.”
“You shall not round the corners of your head, nor mar the corners of your beard.”
The priests “shall not shave off the corners of their beard”.
“Like the good oil on the head, running down on the beard, the beard of Aaron.”
David feigned madness and “let his spittle run down on his beard”.
“Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.”

senses.gloss: beard shaved or plucked, in shame or mourning
senses.definition: The beard cut, shaved or plucked: an outrage done to a man, a sign of mourning, and a figure of judgment.

evidence.note: Hanun “shaved off half their beard” and sent David's servants away.
“The men were greatly ashamed; and the king said, Stay at Jericho until your beard has grown.”
Moab wails: “on all its heads baldness, every beard cut off.”
“Every head is bald and every beard clipped; on all hands gashes, and on the loins sackcloth.”
Eighty men “with their beards shaved and their clothes torn”, bringing offerings to the house of Yahweh.
“I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled out the hair of my head and my beard, and sat appalled.”
Yahweh will shave with a razor hired beyond the River, the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet, “and it shall sweep away the beard also”.
Ezekiel shaves his head and beard with a sword, a sign of Jerusalem's judgment.

senses.definition: The bearded chin of a lion or bear, by which David seized it.

evidence.note: “When it rose against me, I caught it by its beard (בִּזְקָנוֹ) and struck it and killed it.”

senses.definition: The time of being old, when strength fails and hair is gray; Yahweh carries his people to it.

evidence.note: “Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.”
“Even to old age I am he, and to gray hair I will carry you; I have made, and I will bear.”
“Even to old age and gray hair, O God, do not forsake me, until I declare your arm to a generation.”
“Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master after her old age.”
“In the time of Solomon's old age his wives turned away his heart after other gods.”
“In the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.”

evidence.locator: Psa.71.9, זִקְנָה → γήρους; Isa.46.4, זִקְנָה → γήρους; Gen.21.7, זְקֻנָיו → γήρει; Gen.37.3, זְקֻנִים → γήρους

evidence.note: “Elizabeth your kinswoman has also conceived a son in her old age (ἐν γήρᾳ αὐτῆς)”: as Sarah bore Isaac to Abraham's old age (Gen 21:2, 7).

parallels.note: “Gray hair”: old age and gray hair.

words.summary: Only in the plural and only in Genesis, of a son born to a father's old age.

senses.definition: A father's old age, to which a son is born: Isaac to Abraham, Joseph and Benjamin to Jacob.

evidence.note: “Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son לִזְקֻנָיו, at the set time God had spoken.”
“Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne a son to his old age.”
“Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was בֶן־זְקֻנִים to him.”
“An old father, and a son of his old age, a little one.”

phrases.gloss: son of old age, a son born to one's old age

senses.definition: Age, as the cause of failing sight.

evidence.note: “The eyes of Israel were heavy מִזֹּקֶן; he could not see.”

cognates.note: The chin of a man or a beast: the place of the beard, as in the Hebrew of a lion's “beard” (1Sa 17:35). Arabic shows ḏ behind ז.

doctrine.statement: When Moses could not bear the people alone, Yahweh told him to gather seventy men “whom you know that they are elders of the people and its officers”, and said, “I will take of the spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they shall bear the burden of the people with you” (Num 11:16–17). He did so, “and when the spirit rested on them they prophesied”; two who had stayed in the camp prophesied too, and Moses said, “Would that all Yahweh's people were prophets, that Yahweh would put his spirit on them!” (Num 11:25–29). Joel foretold that wish fulfilled: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions” (Joel 3:1), and at Pentecost Peter said, “this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel” (Act 2:16–18). From the verses: the spirit is something Yahweh takes from one man and puts on others, rests on them and pours out, and its work is prophecy; it is Yahweh's own power given to men, which Moses wished on all the people and which came on old and young alike at Pentecost.

Isaiah sees the day when “the moon shall be ashamed and the sun abashed, for Yahweh of Armies will reign in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders, glory” (Isa 24:23): a reign on the earth, in Jerusalem, with elders before him. Zechariah promises, “Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand for very age, and the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing” (Zec 8:4–5), and Isaiah, of the Jerusalem Yahweh creates a rejoicing, that “there shall be no more from there an infant of days, or an old man who does not fill his days” (Isa 65:18–20). In the Revelation twenty-four elders sit on thrones round the throne (Rev 4:4) and sing to the Lamb, “you have made us kings and priests to our God, and we shall reign on the earth” (Rev 5:9–10). From the verses: the kingdom is Yahweh's reign in Zion and Jerusalem, on the earth, shared by those he has redeemed, in a Jerusalem whose old men live out their full days in peace.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key זקנ; no existing entry used it. BDB keys: g.cd.ad adjective, g.cd.ac verb, g.cd.ab זָקָן beard, g.cd.af זִקְנָה, g.cd.ag זְקֻנִים, g.cd.ae זֹקֶן. Shared tokens: the stative verb's perfect and the adjective are spelled alike, so the brief counts 15 qal tokens under the adjective and 20 stemless tokens under the verb; the brief's beard key g.cd.ab also takes Gen 24:2 זְקַן בֵּיתוֹ, which is the adjective (cited there). No personal names from the root in TIPNR. No Biblical Aramaic word: Ezra's elders are שָׂבֵי (Ezr 5:5, 9; 6:7–8, 14), root שׂיב; the Peshitta's are ܩܫܝܫܐ. Jastrow also lists a Jewish Aramaic זְקַן “grow old; make old” written with ז, apparently from the Hebrew (true Aramaic would have ד), so not recorded as a cognate. Sounds: ז is ḏ in Arabic, Ugaritic, Aramaic and Syriac; Akkadian and Phoenician merge it with z. Leads not followed: DULAT and the Ugaritic texts for dqn (El's gray beard, šbt dqnk, KTU 1.3 V and 1.4 V); Payne Smith for Syriac ܕܩܢܐ and any Syriac verb; CAD Z for ziqnu and zaqnu; Eblaite ša-ga-núm and the Modern South Arabian forms (Wiktionary's Proto-Semitic *ḏaḳan-). Open questions: (1) whether “old” comes from “beard” (the bearded, grown man): only Arabic ḏiqn “extremely aged man” beside ḏaqan “chin”, and Akkadian zaqnu “bearded”, point that way; scripture pairs the old man with gray hair (Lev 19:32; Pro 20:29), never with the beard; (2) the doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review; (3) Jol 3:1 old men could be read as elders; filed under old-aged by the parallel with young men.
